topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
source_evidence: A front-end sales load is paid out of the amount of money you have to purchase mutual fund shares. Thus, it decreases the amount of money you have to invest.
question: How does a front-end sales load differ from a back-end sales load in when it is paid and how it affects the purchase of mutual fund shares?
answer: A front-end sales load is deducted when you buy shares, leaving less of your money to invest. A back-end sales load is paid when you redeem (sell back) your shares; if no other purchase fees apply, all your money is used to buy shares initially.
